utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, and I do not want you to mention their names. What was the age group of these women or girls?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 16, 17 years and up at that time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of these young women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were they reacting as they were being taken away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were screaming. They were trying to get away and they were crying.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the men who were taking them away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mladen Mitrovic and Dragoje Cavic and some others that I did not know, but they were all in the camouflage uniforms. They were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see these young women come back to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time if we could have Prosecution Exhibit 203 played from the beginning at the school, please? If you could stop it here, please? Sir, as we are looking at this film here, we see the dom to the right and the toilets to the left. Could you tell us where you were between those two structures when you saw the young women being taken away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I came out of the toilet and maybe I was two or three metres from the toilet when they passed me to the left.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So they passed in front of you or behind you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In front, they were near the dom on that side.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could turn that video off, please? Sir, you said that you saw young women taken away on two occasions. Where were you the second time that you saw this happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the second occasion I was behind the dom.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were these women or girls taken from on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken in the direction of a house which is immediately very close to the restaurant where the Red Cross was.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Again without naming them, did you recognise any of the women or girls who were taken away on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the age group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, mostly they were unmarried girls.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What age group? Were they younger women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, younger.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What ethnic group were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were these women reacting as they were being taken away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same way, crying. They were trying to wrest themselves away from them. They were asking them to let them go.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the men taking these young women away on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised Ratko Ilic and Mladen Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see these young women come back to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If I could have this composite exhibit marked as Prosecution Exhibit 308 for identification? If that could be shown to the Defence and then given to the witness? Sir, do you recognise the buildings depicted in those photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that could be placed on the overhead projector, please? As we look at this Exhibit, what is the building that is shown to the right as you look at the picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was this also the building ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is where the Red Cross was. Here there were soldiers sometimes and the Major.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So if we look to the left side of that building that was the Red Cross office, and if we look to the right side that is where some of the command was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then if we look to the house that is to the left of the cafe, what house is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was the house of Pavle Harasemljuk.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The house of whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pavle Harasemljuk and Tonci. This Pavle is the uncle of Mladen Mitrovic. It is his sister's son, Mladen.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is this the house to which those young women were taken on the second occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The small house that is set back from the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 308 for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 308 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Mujkanovic, while you were at Trnopolje camp did you see any convoys being prepared and departing from the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did see.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How often did you see this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Many times.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did these convoys have escorts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what the escorts wore?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly, they were there together, they were watching as they were being loaded, one they were driving and pushing so that they would pack more into the buses or trucks. They were watching that no man would enter, they were walking around, they were laughing, and like that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall what those escorts wore?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ones -- some wore the camouflage uniforms and those who were in charge of loading were wearing different things, either blue police uniforms, some others had black shirts, still others had -- mostly it was motley, all in all.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever hear these escorts talking among themselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you hear them use any non-local dialects or accents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What dialects or accents did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They spoke Serbian dialect, around Uzice somewhere. They are called Eras. They have a particular accent. They spoke Montenegrin, even Russian.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Uzice, that is located where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Trnopolje camp, did you ever see Dule Tadic in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many times did you see him there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the month that you first saw him, do you recall what month it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What month was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the month of August, the date was 21st.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was happening at the camp on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A convoy was starting.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you on that day when you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was one of the inmates who was looking for an opportunity to get into the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So where were you located when you saw Dule Tadic on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was outside in front of the school building.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was Dule Tadic when you first saw him that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the corner in front of the store.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was he doing when you first saw him that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was standing.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was he alone or was he with others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was with others.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the other people he was with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Part of them I did.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised Goran Borovnica, I recognised Ratko Ilic, I recognised two twin brothers, they were bodyguards, Major Kuruzovic's bodyguards. Their last name is "Balaban". I recognised Mladen Mitrovic. I recognised the son of Pero Curguz, otherwise Pero Curguz, as we call it, was the chief of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw Dule Tadic that day, how far away from you was he when you first saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was standing next to a fence with a policeman of a Serbian nationality. We were friends. I think we remained friends, regardless of what happened. I helped this man. I will not say how or what, and I think that he helped me too. So we were standing and talking.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How far away from you was Dule Tadic as you stood near the fence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 10 to 15 metres, at the most.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what he was wearing that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time he was in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall if he had any facial hair that day when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a beard but not an artistic beard, that means not a long beard. He did have a beard.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On that day when you saw him standing there with these other men, did you have a clear view of him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question very well.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On this day when you saw Dule Tadic standing there with these other men, did you have a clear view of him or did something obstruct your view?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no obstruction. I saw clearly from various points, profiles, as they were being loaded and he was turning around several times.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see after you saw Dule Tadic standing there with the other men? What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The convoy started and they dispersed. Some of them got into cars and they left. They followed the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If I could have 203 played once again, please? Could you back it up, please, and start at the school, at the beginning? If we could stop it here, please? Sir, as you look at this picture on the screen, could you tell us -- is there any way to hold it more still, thank you -- approximately where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot see anything.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you try to hold that frame more still, please? Stop here. Sir, do you see the frame with the store and the fence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Can you see it well enough to tell us approximately where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was standing near that tree.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you inside the fenced area or on the other side of the fenced area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was on the inside, that means to the right, and my friend was to the left.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As we are looking at the store area, can you tell us where Dule Tadic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the very corner.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. We can close off the video, please. Sir, you indicated that on that date you were talking with a Serb friend. What was your Serb friend's position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean what he was before the war or what he was then when we were talking?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What he was then when you were talking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a policeman in a blue uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were talking with your Serb friend, did he tell you anything about the official positions Dule Tadic held at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I raise a matter of law here, your Honour, as this is something that I would say was clearly hearsay (and I am conscious of the judgment that the Court has handed down today, I think, I only saw it briefly this morning) that we would seek to exclude, notwithstanding the judgment, that on the basis of the Rules as they stand, because the evidence that is to be given falls within that category that we would say its probative value is not such that it is possible for the defendant to have a fair trial on this particular matter.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would suggest that this Serb policeman would be in a position to have the information that he imparted to this witness, and that certainly it is relevant information as to what official positions the accused may have held at this time. Therefore, I would suggest that under 89(D) it would be admissible.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. When we return, I will give you a ruling on your objection, unless you want to say anything more? Mr. Kay, do you have anything else to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, there is one matter. We have had no notice of this evidence, so it is not a matter that the Defence have been able to investigate or seek verification of. This is surprise evidence to us.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: How should you have received notice of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In the form of a statement.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You are just saying it was not included in the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. It is fresh material that we are hearing for the first time.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If it comes in, I am sure you will cross-examine about why it was not in the statement and bring that to our attention, but we will consider this. We will stand in recess for 20 minutes and when we return we will give you a ruling.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, you were going to rule on the Defence objection?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Oh, yes. How did we forget about that! The objection is overruled. Once again, as we have indicated in the decision, we do not have a rule that explicitly excludes hearsay. Instead, the Chamber will focus on the probative value. We understand that hearsay because of its very character may be unreliable, but it is not always unreliable. So the objection will be overruled. We consider that on cross-examination, Mr. Kay, you will be able to enquire of the circumstances under which this information was gathered as well as to enquire about its truthfulness, voluntariness and all of the other concerns that at least the majority decision is concerned about. So it is overruled. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Much obliged.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Mujkanovic, before the break I had asked you on this occasion when you first saw Dule Tadic at Trnopolje if your Serb friend had told you anything concerning Dule Tadic's official positions at that time. Had your friend told you anything about the official positions that Dule Tadic held at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did say something.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, only that part of what he said which indicates what official positions Dule Tadic held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told me that Dule Tadic was the secretary of the Local Commune of Kozarac and also that he was a police commander, or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Mujkanovic, if we were to have a closed session, would you be willing to give these the Judges the name of the individual who told you these things about Dule Tadic's position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Of course, now that information would be given to the Judges and the Defence as well ----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- as the accused?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. [To the witness]: Would you also be willing this a closed session to tell the Judges what positions your friend had held in the local area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I would propose is that I complete the rest of my questions with this witness. Then I would ask that we go into closed session for that information, and that then the Defence would be allowed to cross-examine him on the specifics of that incident, including the person's name and position in closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. I am thinking of ways that I can just deal with as limited material as possible within the closed session that does not cause the name of the particular individual to be revealed.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then would we need a closed session? As I recall the testimony and, admittedly, we have been now hearing testimony for several months, I do recall that we have received evidence regarding Mr. Tadic's position as secretary of the Local Commune. I do not recall testimony as to whether he was a police Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have not, no.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: There is no way for me to remember everything. So there is really just one piece of it, perhaps, that will need further enquiry. But are you suggesting a closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I believe the Prosecution feel happier revealing the name in that way.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. We perhaps can handle that this evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Depending upon how long you have on direct and how long you will have on cross, we can just go into closed and finish up. Very good. Continue then.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated that you saw Dule Tadic on two occasions at Trnopolje camp. When was the second time that you saw him at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second time I saw him when I was about to leave and that was in October, on 1st October, when we were off to Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On that occasion where were you when you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were outside lined up in alphabetical order in front of the school towards the road, facing the road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was Dule Tadic when you saw him on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was on the road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw him what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Walking up and down the road. He was just going to and fro. There were very many soldiers on the road and civilians, but he mostly walked up and down.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw him on that day, did you have a clear view of him or was your view obstructed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him clearly.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what he was wearing on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember what he was wearing because I was not thinking about who wore what, but when I would get on to the bus to get away as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall if on that occasion he had any facial hair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a beard but not an artist's beard.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said earlier that by an "artist's beard" you mean a long beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw him on that occasion, what did you see of him? Did you have a full faced view, a profile view? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him both from the profile and I had a frontal view too, but I did not pay much attention to him because I never -- it is enough for me to look up into someone's face, not to look what somebody is wearing, and at that moment all that my attention was riveted on was how to get away from there, and I was really fed up. I was really through with all that I went through there, and every moment of my life was precious to me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you can estimate, how far from you was Dule Tadic on that occasion when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 20 to 25 metres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could once again have Prosecution Exhibit 203 played from the beginning of that Exhibit? If we can stop the video, please, and if we could back it up and go forward very slowly, please? Can we stop the video? Would you please back it up very slowly so we can see the edge of the school? Now forwards just a bit, please? Sir, looking at this -- stop it, please -- video as it is shown here, is this clear enough for you to be able to tell us where you were standing on 1st October when you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were lined up in the alphabetical order, I was down there nearer to the fence, perhaps five or six metres away from the fence, and from the road I was about 20 to 25 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say you were ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere roughly where this fence is broken. I was in this direction, except that we were facing the road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So, sir, when you talk about the fence, you are talking about the fence that is in the foreground of this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You were approximately how many metres behind that fence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not more than 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You were approximately 20 metres behind that fence from the end of the fence, as we see it here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then Dule Tadic was on the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In front of that fence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could shut that off, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry. I have never seen Dule Tadic enter the camp. I do not want to be misinterpreted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So on both occasions that you saw Dule Tadic he was outside the boundaries of the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both times, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, at this time I would ask that you look around the courtroom and see if Dule Tadic from Kozarac is in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please point to him and tell us where he is sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicated) He has a blue suit, a tie, between two policemen.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would note a correct identification of the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, the record will reflect that the witness has identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, when you left Trnopolje on 1st October, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to Karlovac, to Croatia, via Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Mujkanovic, as a result of the attacks that occurred in Opstina Prijedor and the camps that were established there, are any of your family members missing or dead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My family, the Mujkanovic family, in Kozarac is quite large. Those dead, more than 40 have been killed, were killed, but very many are missing. As for my close family, that is as I see them, my brothers, sisters, my brother's children, my sister's children, 13 members of the family. Some were killed. Some had their throat slit. Some I buried myself. Some were buried by others.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, prior to the attack on Kozarac in May 1992, were you a member of any anti-Serb military or paramilitary organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you a member of any organised anti-Serb resistance group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never belonged to any organisation.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could go into closed session at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are you completed with your direct?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, do you want to proceed with cross-examination, then see where we are and then handle it at the end or, if you wish, we can go into closed session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As a result of some instructions that have been given to me, I prefer to hold cross-examination until tomorrow morning. I need to obtain something from the office and prepare it for the Court in readiness for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Does it relate to this piece of information?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we unhook the witness or do not have a translation, we can do our form of approaching the Bench that we discussed a couple of days ago.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, let me just enquire. Mr. Mujkanovic, do you speak English? Do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You neither speak nor understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Miss Hollis, is that procedure acceptable with you so that I can get a better understanding of what Mr. Kay is intending to do if we reserve cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Very good. The witness, Mr. Mujkanovic, would you please take your earphones off? We want to assure that what is being said is not interpreted to the gallery nor to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So, can that be accomplished? OK. Very good. So nothing, the audio will not be going out, is that correct? That is what the technicians tell me. Fine. This is our first time trying this. You may proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Perhaps, your Honour, we should also turn off the headphones?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, during the break I have been given some information which is helpful to the Defence in cross-examination and relates to images of the defendant on a video film as it comes from a television programme. This witness has not actually given that information in evidence, but it is contained within his statement that I do have. To be fair to the witness, I would like to show him that film which contains an image of this defendant looking a particular way.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You do not have that with you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, we do not have it. It has to be dug out, so to speak, from our video film archives. So, if the Prosecution move on to the next witness and I deal with these matters tomorrow, it will be rather more successful rather than breaking off halfway through cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not understand why you do not have this information with you to go forward at this time. Why did you not bring it you with you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I was unaware of the information.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Until?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Literally three minutes before I came into court during the break when I was given certain information which triggered, certainly amongst our recollections, the fact that this was right.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So you did not know about it? Someone else on the team, I gather, knew about it, is that what you are telling me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, not on the Defence team. The defendant, in fact, pointed something out to me and it is ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: How much time do you think you will need for cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Cross-examination will take about 25 to 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Then, Miss Hollis, we will excuse Mr. Mujkanovic this evening. He should report back tomorrow at 10 a.m. We will then begin cross-examination by Mr. Kay at that time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there were some questions I had for him in closed session concerning the identity of the individual and the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then why do we not begin in closed session tomorrow, then you can continue with that and then when you complete your direct, then we will begin with cross-examination and you will have all of the video and everything you need ready to go forward ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- you promise? OK. Very good. Ask the witness to put his earphones on, please. Mr. Mujkanovic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I had asked that you take your earphones off because the lawyers wished to discuss some technical matters with the Judges out of your hearing. We are going to ask that you be excused, that is, that you leave now, but that you return back at 10 a.m. tomorrow morning. We will then continue with your testimony at that time. So you are excused at this point, but you are still under an obligation to return back tomorrow morning at 10 a.m. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. You are excused for the evening.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Who from the Prosecution team will be calling the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The Prosecution calls Mirsad Blazevic. MIRSAD BLAZEVIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you take that oath that is being handed to you, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Sir, would you state your full name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am Mirsad Blazevic, born in Kozarac on 4th January 55.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What part of Kozarac, sir, were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dera.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you go to do your primary school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the primary school in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you attend secondary school in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you then live in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived in Kozarac until my 25th, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you go after that? Where did you live then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I moved to the boundary between Trnopolje and Hrnici, the Local Commune of Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Sir, were you trained as a plumber?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you work up until the war in 1992 as a plumber ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: --- at a company in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you do your military service in 1974 to '75?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was that in Tito's guard of honour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What is your nationality, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosniak Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were you on the date when Trnopolje was attacked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where I was on the day when Trnopolje was attacked?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was near my home, the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What date was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 9th July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Serb Army arrived and began gathering all men from 30 to 70 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened once the men were gathered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From all hamlets, they took us out on to the main road Prijedor/Trnopolje, the lower road, the so-called old road. When I arrived there and my group, I believe we were there last, and there must have been around 200 people lined up in twos. When we were rounded up, we started in the direction of Trnopolje and we were ordered to sing Serb songs, chauvinistic songs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened after that, after your order to sing those songs and you were gathered up, what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were driven, I do not know how far, perhaps 500 metres or kilometres from the place where we had been gathered, and we were stopped by a soldier, that is, he ordered us to halt. We turned, we looked to the right and we turned to the left, and then some counting started. There were seven or eight soldiers walking and counting, each one to himself, and then he would stop by somebody and single him out to that other side. When he had picked out as many as he needed, he ordered us to go ahead. We started and then we heard a burst of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you then loaded on to buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, we continued on foot. We continued again from that place for another 500 metres, more or less, and the column was again stopped, again counted and again people were taken out of the row and they began taking out even some people that I knew, even some of my neighbours they were. Rifat Duracak's two sons, both under age, I think that one was in the primary school, another one in the first grade of the secondary school; Duracak, I believe he worked for Autotransport, his close relative also worked for Autotransport; Esad Mujagic, a driver for Autotransport; Latif Zujic, working for Granja(?) in Prijedor and many others whom I could not all remember. I could not give you now their full names but I do have a list.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After these men were sorted out and taken away and the remainder of the column was there, were you then taken to a place where you were loaded on to buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they also started and they put those men on the same side as the first ones. We were told to keep our heads down. Meanwhile, a soldier with a red beret, I think he was from Gonjenica, and Duca Knezevic -- that is what they called him, "Duca", I do not know his real name -- they were stoned, they were totally drunk, and they started firing at them from their automatic rifles. We were ordered to move forward. We did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And right when we came up to Trnopolje, one could already see the camp, the column was stopped again and again they counted and took out Husein Kahrimanovic, Dusan Knezevic did. In front of a small house there were two bodies. On the right-hand side, the one that we were following down, he ordered me to go to that house. Kahrimanovic started for that house and he came up to those corpses. He was taken aback, so he shouted. He came back. Duca kicked him with a foot in the stomach or in the chest, somewhere there, and the chap cried out something. Duca stepped backward for about two steps and fired the whole burst of the automatic rifle and then ordered us to proceed forward.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, would you ask the witness to speak a little more slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Sir, would you mind speaking just a little more slowly because it becomes too difficult to translate if you speak too fast.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After these events had happened, after these men were sorted out and some were taken away and others were beaten, were you eventually put on a bus where you were taken to firstly the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you arrived at Omarska camp what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no room and they returned us back to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you then put into the camp at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you were in the camp at Keraterm firstly how long were you in that camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I was there from 9th July to about 1st August, maybe a day or two up or down. That is when the Keraterm camp was dissolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you were in that camp did you during that period of time see people who were prisoners in the camp beaten and otherwise mistreated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not quite understand. Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes. When you were in Keraterm camp and during the period of time that you were there, did you see prisoners in the camp who were beaten or otherwise mistreated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you also during that period of time hear people being beaten or otherwise mistreated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both seen with my own eyes and heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you beaten at any stage while you were in the camp at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also I was beaten. I was left without teeth. I only have three teeth left.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you beaten on one occasion or on a number of occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who beat you, do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: With what were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They made a cordon when maybe it was about midnight when we arrived, and as we were getting off the bus one by one we had to get out and they were beating them. There were maybe 15 on each side and through this cordon everybody had to pass, every prisoner, from 13 till, from ages 13 to 80.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you left the camp at Keraterm where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was this to Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What date was it when you arrived at this camp in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around 1st August, I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you went to Trnopolje camp where were you placed, where did you stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the stadium which they fenced with a wire the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you permitted or allowed to move in and about the camp at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, only within the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who was it that prevented you from doing this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the order of the Camp Commander Kuruzovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were there guards at this camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did the guards patrol the perimeter of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were there guard stations or posts located around this camp at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember an incident in September 1992 when five men from Hambarine were arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did this happen when you were in the camp at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened on that occasion when those five men were arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of us were within the perimeter and some of us were within the school building. At the time I was in front of the dome. It was a cultural centre or youth centre and also a restaurant before the war. There I saw the military police bringing five unknown men. They were dirty, unkempt, unshaven.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who were these men brought to first?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These men were brought to and I think they were -- that is right, Major Kuruzovic was not there. It was late afternoon, towards the evening. They were turned over to the waiter. I cannot remember his name now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: This waiter that you cannot remember his name, was he a person local to the Trnopolje area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know where he came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think from Prijedor. There is a part of town that is called Urije.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was his function in the camp at Trnopolje, this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was just a regular guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When these men were turned over to him, what did he then do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He took them to the Local Commune centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were they then taken into the commune centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could you hear something when they were taken inside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we heard, whoever was outside we heard them screaming and we heard the blows and they were begging for mercy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long did this go on for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After about an hour they were taken out hands tied.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How were their hands tied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the back, behind their backs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What were they tied with, could you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think handcuffs, police handcuffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see their condition when they were brought out, the condition of their bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They were in a very severe situation. They were all smeared with blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were they taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards the fish farm beyond the railway station.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you then subsequently lose sight of these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we heard bursts of fire. They were not taken far from the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long after you lost sight of the men did you hear the sound of the bursts of fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately 15 minutes to half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Just to clarify that, by "bursts of fire" you mean rifle fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was the next thing to happen after you heard that sound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They came back, I think his name is Mladen, the waiter, and the other two men whom I did not know, and I saw in front of the entrance of the command, the Red Cross, he was washing the blood from his knee. That is what I saw and others saw too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "they come back", are you talking about the guards and the men, the five men that were taken, or are you just talking about the guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only guards. We never found out anything about the men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know the nationality or ethnic background of these men that were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims. They were from Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know the accused in these proceedings Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How is it that you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know him naturally because I lived there for a long time, so I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You lived in the area of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know of him when you went to school in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see him at school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would see in front of his house, and he was walking around Kozarac. Everybody knew him in Kozarac. He was an athlete and his brothers were athletes too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know where he lived in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as you get into Kozarac on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was married?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know his wife's family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, mostly the father.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His nickname Baja Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During the time that you lived in the Trnopolje/Kozarac area, did you see the accused Dule Tadic on a number of occasions, rarely or was it often?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very rarely because I went to Kozarac seldom. I was going to Prijedor much more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During the period of time that you were staying in the Trnopolje camp, did you ever have an occasion when you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When was this? Can you remember what month it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think somewhere in August, end of August approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him around the corner. There were fences. There were metal fences around the school and I saw him coming out with another uniformed man in a multi-coloured camouflage uniform. He was entering into the premises of the Red Cross and the command quarters where Kuruzovic Slabodan was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you have a good view of Dule Tadic when you saw him on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you then see him on a previous occasion when you were still staying in the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only saw him once in the Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see him outside of the Trnopolje camp at another place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was that place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac near the elementary school and intersection of the Banja Luka/Prijedor old road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember when this was, what time of the month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe around the middle of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What were you doing at this place at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was going to forced labour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who took you to this forced labour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly the guards of the Trnopolje camp took people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They came, the ones who, for instance, knew me, Edem Demirovic(?), Aziz Mujkanovic, Fikret Hujic, to fix the running water for the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How did you get to Kozarac where you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in a truck of my former company.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were there guards with you on this truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was this truck stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who stopped the truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell us as accurately as possible where it was that the truck was stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was stopped at the very school, at that intersection, and he asked us where we were going and what we were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "he asked us", did he ask you or did he ask the guards that were with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked the guards that were guarding us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did they say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a policeman with us. I think he was a Reserve Policeman as far as I know, I do not think he was an active policeman, from the village of Sajaci near Trnopolje. He was like in charge. He was the commander of this guard that was guarding us. He immediately sprung to action with Tadic to explain what we were supposed to do, and Tadic ordered him to unload the supplies that we had. We had the water measuring instruments that count the water expenditure, and we were taking these instruments out of the houses that were destroyed and burnt up, in other words, around the entire Kozarac and the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: These were water meters, were they, that you were collecting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When Tadic ordered you, ordered, I should say, the Reserve Policeman that was with you to unload these water meters, what did the Reserve Policeman say to Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He started to refuse that he, that it was not his, that it was my company's charge and that Tadic was not in charge there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the meantime I was taking out a water meter from a store called Zema and I encountered Boca, Bosko was his name, his neighbour. He told me, because Bosko must have heard this, not to argue with Tadic because he was the Chief Commander of the Special Police Force and not to get into conflict with him, just obey the order, he said to one of the guards that was escorting me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They unloaded all the water meters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was Dule Tadic armed on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: With what was he armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had an automatic rifle with two ----

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During the course of this discussion with the guards that were on your truck, did Dule Tadic do anything with this rifle that he had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: After the meters were unloaded, what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We started going back to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: While the unloading was taking place, did you see anything else happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw a tractor going down Kozarac from the Mrakovica direction loaded with logs and with home furniture. Dule Tadic stopped in front of the tractor and forced it to stop. There were two soldiers in the tractor and one on top of the furniture. They were all carrying automatic rifles. Dule Tadic ordered them to unload all the things that they were carrying. The Serbs started to resist as if they did not want, and I heard with my own ears him say: "Nothing can leave Kozarac, not a piece of a match. I liberated Kozarac and nobody is going to take anything out of Kozarac, only over my dead body." I did not hear anything else. We got back on to the truck and we went back to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On this occasion when you saw Dule Tadic how was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had the camouflage multi-coloured military uniform, and he was trimmed, his hair was trimmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did he have any other arms on his possession, apart from the automatic rifle you have spoken of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see. I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see or can you remember whether or not he was wearing any head wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Apart from the soldier with the name Boca, did you see Dule Tadic with anyone else there on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean on the day when I saw him in Kozarac or until my leaving Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The day when you saw him in Kozarac, was he with anyone else that you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And whom was he with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was with a professional policeman of the civilian police whose name is Babic, son of Dusan Babic. The police were in the elementary school and I saw Babic in front of the school building and the other policemen too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Earlier in your evidence you spoke of seeing Tadic Dule Tadic at the camp in Trnopolje in September. When you saw him on that occasion do you recall how he was dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also the multi-coloured camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On that occasion did you see whether or not he was carrying any arms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When were you released from Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly on October 1st 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember the names of any of the guards who were guarding the camp at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A very small number.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us the names of any of those guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Pero Jauz, Gavro Gajic, Mladen that waiter I cannot remember his name but I know his first name was Mladen. Right now I cannot name any others.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know any guards with the name Karajica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew of him but I did not see him. You mean the name? Do you have a name?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, I am asking you whether you knew a guard there that had the name Karajica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you now, please, look around the courtroom for me and can you tell me if you see the person that you know and recognise as Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicated).

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You pointed to that person. Would you please describe for the transcript where he is seated and how he is dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. He is sitting between two policemen and he is looking me in the eyes and he has a, you know, a black suit and a tie and a shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Might the record reflect, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, the record will reflect that the witness identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand you. I did not hear well?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann just said that he had no further questions. We will adjourn until tomorrow at 10 a.m. When we begin tomorrow at 10 a.m. we will be in closed session. Miss Hollis, you will continue with Mr. Mujkanovic and then there will be cross-examination. Then we will continue with this witness in open session or even continue with Mr. Mujkanovic in open session when we resolve that one matter. Thank you. We will adjourn until tomorrow at 10 a.m. (5.30 p.m.). (The court adjourned until the following day). 21
